tools.name: check_design
tools.description: Check a page's HTML/CSS/copy/interaction for the patterns that make AI-generated work read as generic: default fonts, soft tech gradients, pill+arrow buttons, eyebrow labels, a composition with no real width/background variation across sections, uniform card grids, copy tells (AI vocabulary, negativ

tools.name: check_copy
tools.description: Check marketing or outreach copy (an email, a landing-page draft, a pitch, a social post) for the tells that make it read as AI-generated: cliché vocabulary (delve, unlock, empower, seamlessly integrate, etc.), negative-parallel framing ("not just X, but Y"), hedge words, heavy em-dash use, and diag

tools.name: check_code
tools.description: Check a source file or diff for AI 'tells' left in comments: narrating fulfilling a request instead of describing the code ("as requested," "I've added," "here's the updated version") and hedge words. These reveal there was a conversation behind the change that a later reader has no access to. Call

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_design, check_copy, check_code · Private data: check_code · Public sink: check_copy.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_design, check_copy, check_code · Private data: check_code · Public sink: check_copy

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
